record.original_question: (D. Segal). A group word w is said to be concise in a class C of groups if for every group G in C such that the set Gw of word values of w in G is finite, the verbal subgroup w(G) = ⟨Gw ⟩ is also finite(see also Archive 2.45). Is every word concise in the class of residually finite groups? See(D. Segal, Words. Notes on verbal width in groups, Cambridge Univ. Press, 2009) for a partial solution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be the free group on countably many generators $x_1, x_2, \ldots$, and let $w \in F$ be a group word. For a group $G$, define the set of $w$-values in $G$ by
$$G_w = \{\, w(g_1, \ldots, g_n)^{\pm 1} : g_1, \ldots, g_n \in G \,\},$$
and the verbal subgroup $w(G) = \langle G_w \rangle$.

The word $w$ is called concise in a class $\mathcal{C}$ of groups if, for every $G \in \mathcal{C}$ such that $G_w$ is finite, the verbal subgroup $w(G)$ is also finite.

A group $G$ is residually finite if for every $1 \neq g \in G$ there exists a normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ of finite index with $g \notin N$.

Question: Is every group word $w$ concise in the class of residually finite groups? Equivalently, does every residually finite group $G$ in which the set $G_w$ of values of a word $w$ is finite necessarily have a finite verbal subgroup $w(G)$?
artifact.category_tag: Concise words in residually finite groups
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every word is concise in the class of residually finite groups (equivalently, in profinite groups) remains open and is regarded as the central conjecture on this topic. Partial results are known: many specific families of words have been shown to be concise in residually finite groups, including Engel words and generalizations, and any word expressible as a commutator of two non-commutator words. An ERC project (GroupConciseness) and several recent papers (2018–2025) explicitly state the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: On words that are concise in residually finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Hall's question whether every word is concise remains wide open in the class of residually finite groups.
status_evidence.claim: The conciseness question is open for residually finite groups.

status_evidence.title: Words of Engel type are concise in residually finite groups
status_evidence.snippet: Various Engel-type words shown to be concise in residually finite groups.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: specific word families are concise in residually finite groups.

status_evidence.title: GroupConciseness ERC project
status_evidence.snippet: Whether all words are concise in profinite/residually finite groups is the main open conjecture in the topic.
status_evidence.claim: Problem currently open and active research focus.
